lawyer: Golam Rabbani, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
parties:
Boktar Ali (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Anjuara Begum and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the order No. 21 dated 30-8-2001 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Lalmonirhat in Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2000 (brought under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure) allowing an application made under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and setting aside the order dated 4-7-2001 passed by the said Court allowing a prayer under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting aside his own judgment and order dated 30-4-2000 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998 allowing the said appeal and setting aside the judgment and order dated 24-9-1998 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1994 by Senior Assistant Judge, Lalmonirhat, Sadar allowing pre-emption case should not be set aside. 

 2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that, the petitioner being preemptor filed a Miscellaneous case being No. 15 of 1994 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Lalmonirhat seeking for pre-emption of the land transferred by the Kabala dated 23-11-1993 executed and registered by the pre-emptee No. 3 in favour of pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 stating a nutshell that the jote under pre-emption belonged to Amir Ullah and others; that one of the owners of the jote named Taiman Bewan died after promulgation of the Muslim Family Law of Inheritance leaving behind her predeceased daughter Ayesha's son named Taleb and a daughter named Nabijan; that Nabijan died leaving behind a daughter named Momena who sold 40 1/2 decimals of land by a kabala dated 18-10-1977 in favour of the pre-emptor and his brothers the pre-emptee Nos. 21(0 24; that by that kabala the pre-emptor became a co-sharer to the case holding; that the pre-emptee No. 3 in collusion with the pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 transferred the land under pre-emption by the kabala dated 23-11-1993; that no notice of the said kabala was served upon the pre-emptor; that the pre-emptor came to know about the said kabala on 1-3-1994 and got the certified copy of the said kabala on 23-3-1994; that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are stranger purchasers; that the pre-emptor purchased from plot No. 1222 and by the kabala under pre-emption the land of plot No. 1222 was shown to have been transferred and that with these statements the pre-emption case was filed. 

 3. The pre-emptee Nos. 1 and 2 filed a written statement and contested the pre-emption case only keeping confined their contest stating, inter cilia, that Taiman Bewa died before 1961 and thereby the pre-emptor by the kabala dated 18-10-1977 from Momena did not acquire the status of a co-sharer; that the pre-emptor in their written objection admitted the fact CS recorded tenant Ibrahim died leaving behind widow Taiman and a daughter Ayesha; that during pre-emptory hearing, evidence was adduced to the effect that Ayesha died after 6 years of the liberation of Bangladesh. 

 4. The pre-emptor adduced 3 PWs and the pre-emptee did not adduce any evidence by themselves to deny the pre-emptor's case. 

 6. The pre-emptee preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998 and during pendency of the appeal, the pre-emptee opposite party Nos. I and 2 by practising fraud upon the Court managed to pen through their admitted fact in their written objection regarding co-sharership of Ayesha and by practising fraud upon the Court got heard the appeal; that the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Lalmonirhat by order dated 30-4-2000 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and order dated 24-9-1998 passed in Miscellaneous case No. 15 of 1994. 

 7. The pre-emptor on coming to know about the fact filed an application under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for review of the order dated 30-4-2000 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998. 8. The review application was heard on contest and was allowed by order dated 4-7-2001. Thereafter the pre-emptee filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the order dated 4-7-2001. 9. The learned Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Lalmonirhat entertained the application and allowed the same by the impugned order dated 30-08-2001. 10. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment dated 30-8-2001, the petitioner filed this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 12. Mr Golam Rabbani, cited the decision in the case of Sabiranessa vs Kabir Ahmed reported in 49 DLR 347 and the case of Amirunnesa vs Abdul Mannar; reported in 3 BLC 404 in support of his contention. 

 14. It appears from the evidence on record that the learned Assistant Judge hearing both parties and on consideration of materials on record allowed the pre-emption by his judgment and order dated 24-9-1998 against which Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998 was preferred. It is alleged by pre-emptor petitioner that during pendency of the appeal, the pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 by practising fraud upon the Court managed to pen-through their admitted fact stated in their written objection regarding co-sharer ship of Ayesha and by practising fraud upon the Court, the opposite party obtained the judgment and order dated 30-4-2000. The pre-emptor petitioner came to know about said fact and filed an application under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reviewing the order dated .30-4-2000 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998 and the review application was heard on contest and was allowed by order dated 4-7-2001. 

 16. Since the review application was allowed by order dated 4-7-2001 which is a final order it cannot be interfered by the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In arriving at this decision reliance is placed in the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 51 (Abdur Rahman vs Sultan). 

 17. When the review application under Order XLVII, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure was preferred against the order dated 30-4-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 30 of 1998 and which was finally allowed by order dated 4-7-2001, after giving such order the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not tenable in law. Because the pre-emptee opposite parties' application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not at all maintainable by law. The pre-emptee opposite parties could prefer a revision against the order dated 4-7-2001. An avenue was opened in that line. 

 19. The preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities of this Subcontinent are that if an alternative remedy is available in the statute, the inherent power of this sort cannot be invoked. In this case since the alternative-remedy of revision was available in the statute then the pre-emptees opposite parties cannot file an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In such case the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Lalmonirhat cannot exercise inherent power. Because he cannot sit over his own judgment being functus officio.
